title: Nephritic vs Nephrotic, Stones, and the Failing Kidney

questions.stem: A swollen child, foamy urine, and a quiet sediment (no red-cell casts) is most consistent with:

options.text: Nephrotic disease, and in a child think minimal change

questions.explanation: Heavy protein and swelling without a bloody sediment is nephrotic. In a child, think minimal change.

questions.stem: An adult with heavy protein and spike deposits on biopsy most likely has:
questions.explanation: Membranous nephropathy is the classic adult nephrotic pattern with spikes.

questions.stem: A painful stone that does not show on a plain film is most often:
questions.explanation: Uric acid stones are radiolucent on a plain film.

questions.stem: Nephrotic-range protein is commonly taught as about:
questions.explanation: The classic cutoff is about 3.5 grams a day or more.

questions.stem: Adult polycystic kidney disease is especially associated with:

options.text: Liver fibrosis as the defining childhood clue
Hypertension and a risk of brain aneurysms
Radiolucent uric acid stones in every case

questions.explanation: The adult form brings large kidneys, hypertension, and intracranial aneurysm risk. The infantile form brings liver fibrosis.

questions.stem: Infantile (autosomal-recessive) polycystic kidney disease is especially associated with:

options.text: Only brain aneurysms, never liver disease
A purely nephritic sediment in every case

questions.explanation: The infantile form is a different pattern and brings hepatic fibrosis.

questions.stem: Renal-artery stenosis typically raises blood pressure through:
questions.explanation: The under-perfused kidney pours out renin.

questions.stem: In chronic kidney mineral disease, which pair typically rises together?

options.text: Only free water and no ions
Only uric acid visibility on a plain film

questions.explanation: When the kidney cannot clear phosphate, phosphate rises and parathyroid hormone follows.

questions.stem: Red-cell casts and modest protein, with a high blood pressure, point first to:

options.text: Minimal change in a toddler, first thought

questions.explanation: Blood and red-cell casts are nephritic, not heavy-protein nephrotic disease.

options.text: Minimal change often presents in children and the light microscope can look almost normal.
Membranous nephropathy is a classic adult nephrotic pattern with spikes.
Uric acid stones always light up on a plain film.
Adult and infantile polycystic disease are the same gene at two ages.

questions.explanation: Uric acid stones hide on a plain film. Adult and infantile polycystic diseases are different patterns.
